extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners, and patent practitioners handling ex parte reexamination proceedings before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for requesting, examining, and prosecuting ex parte reexamination proceedings at the USPTO, including Office action content, timing, service, extensions, and special issues (Portola Packaging, foreign language references, cumulative references, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing prior art status for previously-cited references
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reference was previously presented in prosecution but its status as prior art was not adequately established, a reexamination request should explain how and why the reference actually qualifies as prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of appropriate showings include: (i) verifying the date of the reference; (ii) undermining the sufficiency of a declaration filed under 37 CFR 1.131(a) (by showing an inaccuracy/mistake of fact in the declaration); or (iii) explaining the correct filing date accorded a claim where the issue was not previously addressed. See Heinl v. Godici for precedent that reexamination may proceed if prior art status is now established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign language reference translation completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: If a foreign-language prior art reference was cited/discussed previously but never completely and accurately translated into English, a reexamination request that provides a complete and accurate translation explaining how the reference meets claim requirements may justify reliance on that reference in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requester should explain why a more complete and accurate translation actually teaches what is required by the patent claims; Portola Packaging does not necessarily prohibit reexamination when a fuller translation establishes prior art content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of cumulative/repetitive references
rubrics_metrics.description: References that are substantially repetitive (i.e., substantially reiterate verbatim the teachings of a previously applied or discussed reference) are considered cumulative and, under Portola Packaging, may be excluded from reexamination if they add nothing substantive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'cumulative' or 'repetitive' reference reiterates verbatim teachings of an earlier applied/discussed reference even if title or citation differs. Such exclusions are expected to be rare because most references teach additional information or present it differently even on the same subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required notices when terminating/withdrawing under Portola Packaging
rubrics_metrics.description: When prosecution is terminated or rejections withdrawn to comply with In re Portola Packaging, the Office must include specific language in Notices of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate or in Office actions withdrawing rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example required wording for termination: 'The prosecution of this reexamination is terminated based on In re Portola Packaging, Inc., 110 F.3d 786, 42 USPQ2d 1295 (Fed. Cir. 1997). No patentability determination has been made in this reexamination proceeding.' Example wording for withdrawn rejections: 'The rejection(s) based upon _______ is/are withdrawn in view of In re Portola Packaging, Inc., ... No patentability determination of the claims of the patent in view of such prior art has been made in this reexamination proceeding.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of res judicata and collateral estoppel
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims finally held valid by a federal court after all appeals will be withdrawn from consideration and not reexamined; collateral estoppel may be applied to resolve particular issues decided in court that are applicable to the claims under reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP §§2242 and 2286 govern how court decisions precluding reexamination (res judicata) or applying collateral estoppel affect reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special dispatch timelines and priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination proceedings must be conducted with 'special dispatch.' The examiner’s first action on the merits should be completed within specified short timeframes and certain reexaminations have priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First action should be completed within 1 month of the filing date of the requester’s reply (37 CFR 1.535) or the patent owner’s statement (37 CFR 1.530) if no requester, with mailing within 6 weeks after the appropriate filing/due date. Cases involved in litigation (reexaminations or reissues) have priority over others; non‑litigated reexaminations have priority over other cases except litigated reexaminations/reissues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for first and subsequent Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s first Office action on the merits should clearly establish the issues between the examiner and patent owner and be sufficiently detailed to permit a proper final action subsequently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first action must set forth pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to each claim; if the request includes claim charts, the examiner may incorporate them but must carefully review to ensure incorporated items clearly and completely address patentability. Subsequent actions must address all patent owner responses. If claims are found patentable, the examiner should indicate why in a manner similar to reasons for allowance (MPEP §1302.14) and may refer to record portions establishing patentability. The first action should caution the patent owner that a complete response is required because the next action is expected to be final and that 37 CFR 1.116(b) requirements will be strictly enforced after final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of patent owner statements in claim interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner relies upon a patent owner statement submitted under 37 CFR 1.501(a)(2) in the detailed explanation, the reexamination requester must explain how that statement is being used to determine the proper meaning of a patent claim in connection with prior art applied to that claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: That explanation will be considered by the Office in drafting the Office action to determine the scope of the claims subject to reexamination; reliance on such statements must be explicit and supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for changing patent title during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Title changes are generally unnecessary in reexamination; if necessary, the patent owner should be notified early and any change to the title in connection with a Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate may only be done by formal Examiner’s Amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing the title and merely initialing the change is NOT permitted in reexamination. Notify patent owner as early as possible to provide an amendment changing the title as part of an Office Action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone conference practice and recordation
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may indicate that a telephone conference with the patent owner’s representative may lead to agreement and may prepare or revise an Office action around such a conference; appropriate conferee initials are required when a conference confirms the examiner’s preliminary decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under this practice the examiner may contact the patent owner’s representative within about 2 weeks to prepare the representative. If a conference confirms a preliminary decision to reject/allow claims, the Office action shall be issued and signed by the examiner, with two or more other conferees initialing the action as 'conferee' to indicate presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of dependent claims in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling of dependent claims depends on whether the base (independent) claim is an unamended base claim appearing in the patent or a new/amended base claim introduced in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an unamended base patent claim (as it appears in the patent) is rejected or canceled, any claim directly/indirectly dependent thereon should be confirmed or allowed if otherwise allowable; do not object/reject solely because it depends on a rejected/canceled patent claim and do not require rewriting into independent form. If a new base claim (one not appearing in the patent) has been canceled, a claim depending thereon should be rejected as indefinite. If a new base claim or amended patent claim is rejected, a claim dependent thereon should be objected to if otherwise patentable and require rewriting the dependent claim in independent form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory response periods and shortened periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination proceedings generally use shortened statutory periods for responses; default is 2 months, but exceptions and authorized shortened periods exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A shortened statutory period of 2 months is set for responses, except where reexamination results from a court order or litigation is stayed for purposes of reexamination (shortened to 1 month). If litigation is concurrent and the reexamination has been pending >1 year, certain officials may approve a 1‑month shortened statutory period for Office actions. The 2‑month statutory period for a patent owner statement under 37 CFR 1.530 is fixed by statute (35 U.S.C. 304) and cannot be lessened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing and transmittal procedures for Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Office actions must be mailed using PALM-printed identifying information and appropriate transmittal forms; third-party requesters and partial patent owners receive copies per procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PALM printer to print reexamination file ID and mailing address (usually patent owner’s representative). Provide PTOL‑465 transmittal form for each partial patent owner and for third‑party requesters; all actions in a third‑party requester ex parte reexamination must have a copy mailed to the third‑party requester. Documents must reflect service or may be refused consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time procedures and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time in ex parte reexamination are permitted only for sufficient cause, must be filed on or before the due date, and require the petition fee; the applicable regulatory provision is 37 CFR 1.550(c), not 37 CFR 1.136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request must (A) be filed on or before the due date, (B) set forth sufficient reason (including factual accounting of reasonably diligent behavior by those preparing the response), and (C) be accompanied by the petition fee in §1.17(g). Requests are decided by the CRU Director or TC Director. First requests usually granted for a reasonable time (usually 1 month); second/subsequent or more-than-1-month requests granted only in extraordinary situations. Requests filed before decision to grant/deny reexamination are denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-extendability of statutory reply periods for third-party requester
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory 2‑month period for a third‑party requester's reply under 37 CFR 1.535 to the patent owner’s statement cannot be extended under any circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 2‑month period is statutory (35 U.S.C. 304) and cannot be waived or extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-final practice and automatic 1-month extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a timely first response to a final rejection in a reexamination with a shortened statutory period is treated as including a request for a 1‑month extension; total extension cannot exceed 6 months from mailing date of final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The automatic 1‑month extension applies only to the first response after final and not once a Notice of Appeal is filed. The advisory action form PTOL-467 can be used to grant an extension up to 6 months (fill in integer months 2–6). If the patent owner elects to file a subsequent amendment, it must place the reexamination in condition for allowance or prosecution will terminate under 37 CFR 1.550(d) unless an appeal was filed before expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of affidavits submitted after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits filed after final rejection are treated like amendments after final; granting an extension to submit an affidavit does not guarantee its entry and the affidavit may be denied if the showing is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may question why the affidavit is now necessary and why it was not earlier presented; admission or refusal of the affidavit does not save prosecution from termination. See In re Affidavit Filed After Final Rejection precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for patent owner replies to Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies must be written and must distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors in the examiner’s action, reply to every ground of objection/rejection, and present arguments showing specific distinctions believed to render the claims patentable over applied references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply must appear to be a bona fide attempt to advance the application or reexamination to final action. A general allegation that the claims define a patentable invention without specific argument does not comply. In amending, the applicant must clearly point out the patentable novelty and show how amendments avoid references or objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental reply entry conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental replies are not entered as a matter of right except in limited categories; the Office may enter a supplemental reply only when it is clearly limited to specified subjects or filed while Office action is suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories (37 CFR 1.111(a)(2)(i)) permitting entry include: (A) cancellation of claim(s); (B) adoption of examiner suggestions; (C) placement in condition for allowance; (D) reply to an Office requirement made after the first reply was filed; (E) correction of informalities (typographical errors); (F) simplification of issues for appeal. A supplemental reply filed during a suspension period (§1.103(a) or (c)) will be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: General procedural rules under 37 CFR 1.550 (conduct of ex parte reexamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte reexaminations are to be conducted with special dispatch, provide minimum response periods, and include rules on what submissions are permitted and how participation of third‑party requesters is limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points: (a) proceedings conducted with special dispatch and will result in issuance of ex parte reexamination certificate under §1.570; (b) patent owner given at least 30 days to respond to any Office action and may submit statements, proposed amendments, or new claims to place patent in allowable condition; (c) extensions only for sufficient cause with petition fee; (d) failure to file timely/appropriate response leads to terminated prosecution and issuance of certificate per last Office action; (e) reexamination requester will be sent copies of Office actions and its active participation ends with the reply under §1.535 — no further submissions will be considered except as permitted by §§1.510, 1.535, or entered prior to order for reexamination per §1.525; (f) documents filed after order must meet requirements of §1.501(a); (g) documents filed by either party must be served on the other per §1.248 or may be refused consideration.
